title: Distributed Microservices System (Event-Driven)
problem: Need for scalable, independently deployable backend services with loose coupling and fault tolerance

architecture.description: Six independently deployable Spring Boot microservices communicating via Apache Kafka, secured by Keycloak/OAuth2, with observability through Prometheus/Grafana

decisions.decision: Use Spring Cloud Netflix Eureka for service discovery
decisions.tradeOffs: Eureka offers tight Spring Boot integration but adds JVM-based infrastructure overhead

decisions.decision: Use Apache Kafka for event-driven communication
decisions.tradeOffs: Kafka provides high throughput and replayability but requires operational expertise for ZooKeeper management

decisions.decision: Implement Resilience4j for fault tolerance
decisions.tradeOffs: Resilience4j is lightweight and modular but adds dependency overhead

improvements: Implement schema registry for Kafka topics
Add distributed tracing with Jaeger or Zipkin

title: Three-Tier App on AWS EKS with GitOps
problem: Need for reproducible, observable cloud infrastructure with automated deployment pipelines

architecture.description: React frontend, Node.js API, MongoDB database deployed as containerized workloads on AWS EKS via Argo CD GitOps

decisions.decision: Use Argo CD for GitOps continuous delivery
decisions.tradeOffs: Argo CD provides Kubernetes-native declarative deployments but requires learning GitOps principles

decisions.decision: Use AWS EKS for managed Kubernetes
decisions.tradeOffs: EKS reduces operational burden but offers less control than self-managed clusters

decisions.decision: Use MongoDB StatefulSet with PersistentVolumes
decisions.tradeOffs: StatefulSets provide stable network identities and persistent storage but add complexity to backup/restore procedures

improvements: Add service mesh (Istio/Linkerd) for traffic management
Add horizontal pod autoscaling based on custom metrics

title: BidSafe - Real-Time Bidding Platform with Concurrency Safety
problem: Race conditions in concurrent bidding systems leading to duplicate bids, inventory overselling, and financial discrepancies

architecture.description: Spring Boot API with layered locking strategy (pessimistic + optimistic + Redis distributed) for bid processing safety

decisions.decision: Implement triple-layer locking strategy
decisions.tradeOffs: Multiple locking mechanisms add complexity but provide redundant safety guarantees

decisions.decision: Use Idempotency-Key for exactly-once processing
decisions.tradeOffs: Idempotency-Key provides explicit deduplication but requires client cooperation

decisions.decision: Use Bucket4j for rate limiting
decisions.tradeOffs: Bucket4j offers in-memory simplicity but doesn't scale to multiple instances without Redis backend

improvements: Implement snapshot isolation for audit trails

title: Cloud-Native CI/CD Pipeline for Spring Boot
problem: Manual, error-prone deployment processes slowing down release cycles and increasing failure rates

architecture.description: Jenkins/GitLab CI/CD pipeline automating build, test, security scan, containerization, and deployment to AWS EC2

decisions.decision: Use Jenkins/GitLab for CI/CD orchestration
decisions.tradeOffs: Self-hosted runners provide full control but require maintenance overhead

decisions.decision: Integrate SonarQube for static code analysis
decisions.tradeOffs: SonarQube provides comprehensive quality gates but adds pipeline execution time

decisions.decision: Use NGINX as reverse proxy with SSL termination
decisions.tradeOffs: NGINX offers high performance and flexibility but requires manual SSL certificate management

improvements: Implement pipeline caching for faster builds
Add automated rollback on deployment failure

title: BudgetStack - Flask Expense Tracker with Automated CI/CD
problem: Manual deployment processes for web applications causing delays and inconsistent environments

architecture.description: Flask/Mysql application with automated deployment via GitHub Webhooks → GitHub Actions → Jenkins → EC2

decisions.decision: Use GitHub Webhooks to trigger CI/CD pipeline
decisions.tradeOffs: Webhook-based triggering provides flexibility but adds dependency on GitHub availability

decisions.decision: Implement swap space and health checks for EC2
decisions.tradeOffs: Swap + health checks is cost-effective but requires monitoring and tuning

decisions.decision: Use Docker Compose for local development
decisions.tradeOffs: Docker Compose ensures environment consistency but adds container overhead

title: Automated Examination System
problem: Manual examination processes are time-consuming, error-prone, and lack instant feedback mechanisms

architecture.description: Role-based examination system with Spring Boot REST backend and React frontend

decisions.decision: Use Agile/Scrum methodology for team coordination
decisions.tradeOffs: Agile/Scrum provides adaptability but requires disciplined ceremony adherence

decisions.decision: Use JWT for stateless authentication
decisions.tradeOffs: JWT enables horizontal scaling but requires secure secret key management

decisions.decision: Use Selenium WebDriver for end-to-end testing
decisions.tradeOffs: Selenium provides cross-browser testing but has steeper learning curve and flakiness

improvements: Add adaptive question difficulty based on user performance
Implement proctoring features for remote exams

title: AI-Powered Research Assistant
problem: Researchers spend excessive time manually summarizing papers and extracting key insights from academic literature

architecture.description: Chrome Extension frontend with reactive Spring Boot backend integrating Google Gemini API

decisions.decision: Use Chrome Extension for browser integration
decisions.tradeOffs: Chrome Extension provides contextual help but is limited to Chrome browser

decisions.decision: Use Google Gemini API for AI summarization
decisions.tradeOffs: Gemini offers strong reasoning capabilities but requires API usage and has rate limits

decisions.decision: Use Spring WebFlux for reactive backend
decisions.tradeOffs: WebFlux provides non-blocking I/O but has steeper learning curve

improvements: Add citation extraction and bibliography generation
Add support for multiple document formats (PDF, EPUB)
Implement offline mode with local caching

title: Scribbly Note Sharing Platform
problem: Students and professionals lack efficient ways to share, organize, and collaborate on lecture notes and study materials

architecture.description: Secure RESTful backend with MVC architecture, JWT authentication, and cloud storage integration

decisions.decision: Use MVC architecture for separation of concerns
decisions.tradeOffs: MVC provides clear structure but may not scale to extremely high complexity

decisions.decision: Use JWT for stateless authentication
decisions.tradeOffs: JWT enables horizontal scaling but requires secure secret key management

decisions.decision: Use Cloudinary for media storage and transformation
decisions.tradeOffs: Cloudinary provides rich media features but adds third-party dependency and cost

improvements: Implement spell check and grammar suggestions
